actions.action: Check whether the small plant at the base is rooted separately
Soak the root ball thoroughly until water drains
Water again only when the top 1–2 inches of soil are dry (check soil)
Use filtered water or rainwater if tap water is hard or treated
Move the plant to bright indirect light, a few feet back from the south window
Alternatively, put up a sheer curtain to diffuse the window light
Acclimate the plant gradually to the brighter light over 2–3 weeks
Stop the grow light or use it only as a supplement
Inspect leaf undersides and leaf joints for mealybugs, scale and spider mites
Wipe the leaves with a damp cloth
If pests are found, treat with insecticidal soap
Cut off badly damaged or fully brown leaves at the base
Keep the plant away from cold drafts and cold glass in winter
Repot in spring into a pot 1–2 inches larger
Use potting mix with added perlite or pumice, or a well-draining cactus mix
When repotting, trim any mushy, dark roots
Optionally cut back a tall, bare trunk in spring

reason: The answer misidentifies the Crinum lily as a Dracaena and blames underwatering, light shock and pests, so the diagnosis is wrong. Its advice to pull the plant back from the sunny window, its reassurance that temperatures are fine, and its suggestion to cut back the 'trunk' run counter to the light and warmth a Crinum needs, which makes it harmful.
